memory_candidates.content: This agent system has three distinct context-loading tiers, not two: (1) CLAUDE.md's own @-imports, resolved by the harness at session start; (2) a SKILL.md or agent-definition .md body, read in full whenever the Skill/Agent tool invokes it -- genuinely eager at invocation time even though it is not session-start eager, and any @-prefixed reference written INSIDE such a body is NOT harness-expanded (it's stylistic, not the real import syntax); (3) on-demand, a plain path cited in prose that a consumer reads explicitly only if needed. When auditing whether some context 'actually loads', check which tier the citing location sits in before concluding a pointer is dead -- a pointer dead at tier 1 may have its content duplicated and load-bearing at tier 2.

Pattern for resolving an 'is this safety doc actually enforced' question: grep every consumer skill/agent body for citations of the target file by name. If zero citations exist but the file's substantive content (specific rules, constants, thresholds) is found duplicated verbatim/near-verbatim inside the consumer bodies themselves, the file is a human-facing synthesis/onboarding doc, not a runtime dependency -- the fix is documenting that role explicitly, not eager-loading the file.
